places.name: La Trattoria Ocean Drive
places.note: Italian, right up the block. Reliably good and the happy hour is the draw — two-for-one cocktails, patio seating facing the water.

places.name: IL Giardino
places.note: Casual Italian two doors down from La Trattoria. Big drinks, hookah, open until 2 AM. Service reviews are uneven — go for the convenience and the late hours, not a special meal.

places.name: Cafe Americano
places.note: Best nearby option for a real breakfast. Oceanfront tables, fresh-squeezed juice, closes at 4 PM so it's a morning-only play.

places.name: Il Pastaiolo
places.note: One of the highest-rated restaurants in the neighborhood and a three-minute walk. Pasta made in house, tableside tiramisu. Order tap water unless you want a twelve-dollar bottle.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 12:00 PM – 11:45 PM · Fri–Sat until 12:45 AM

places.name: Mercato della Pescheria
places.note: Italian seafood with an oyster bar, set on Española Way — the Mediterranean-style pedestrian block. Good group energy and a change of scenery from Ocean Drive without going far.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11:30 AM – 11:30 PM · Fri–Sat until 12:00 AM

places.name: Sola Miami Beach
places.note: Mexican and steak with a brunch show and bottomless mimosas. Seating is outdoors, which is the whole appeal and also the main complaint.
places.hours: Mon 8:00 AM – 12:00 AM · Fri–Sat until 2:00 AM

places.name: Montana's Miami Beach
places.note: Open 8 AM to 2 AM, so it covers breakfast through last call. Good when you want food alongside music rather than a sit-down dinner.

places.name: Osteria del Mar
places.note: Oceanfront Italian. Reviews split hard — the ceviche and oysters get praise, the pizza gets called a tourist trap. Fine for drinks and a starter, less so for a full dinner.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 8:00 AM – 11:00 PM · Fri–Sat until 12:00 AM

places.name: Meet Dalia
places.note: Mediterranean and seafood, open to 1 AM on weekends. The branzino and spicy shrimp pasta are the standouts. Good people-watching from the patio.
places.hours: Sun–Wed 7:00 AM – 12:00 AM · Thu–Sat until 1:00 AM

places.name: Santorini by Georgios
places.note: Greek, across from the Delano. Lamb chops and cocktails come up in review after review. Indoor and outdoor seating, open early and late.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 7:00 AM – 11:00 PM · Fri–Sat until 12:00 AM

places.name: Forte dei Marmi
places.note: Upscale Italian down in South of Fifth. Truffle pasta is the signature. Expensive, and reviews argue about whether it earns it — book it as the splurge night or skip it.

places.name: Joe's Stone Crab
places.note: The Miami institution, over a century old. Stone crab claws with mustard sauce, key lime pie, white tablecloths. No reservations for the main room — expect a long wait, or use the takeaway counter next door for the same food without the ceremony.

places.name: Monty's Sunset
places.note: Waterfront bar and grill at the marina with a pool, live music, and free parking — genuinely rare here. Best used as a laid-back sunset happy hour, not a destination dinner.

places.name: The Roof at Esme Hotel
places.note: The closest rooftop and the most relaxed one. Craft cocktails, no crush of people, live jazz on Sunday nights. Closes at 10 PM, so it's an early-evening stop.

places.name: The Clevelander
places.note: The pool-bar landmark on Ocean Drive. Loud, touristy, and exactly what it advertises. Best in the afternoon by the pool; open to 5 AM Thursday through Saturday.
places.hours: Mon–Wed 11:00 AM – 2:00 AM · Thu–Sat until 5:00 AM

places.name: Carnaval Rooftop
places.note: Rooftop with a DJ, a small stage, and hookah. Opens at 7 PM on weekdays and runs to 5 AM. Food is overpriced — come for the drinks and the view.
places.hours: Mon–Thu 7:00 PM – 5:00 AM · Fri–Sun from 11:00 AM

places.name: Mango's South Beach
places.note: Live music, salsa dancing, and a full floor show. Dinner-and-show format works well for a group. Cover charge for men, table minimums on busy nights.

places.name: Watr at the 1 Rooftop
places.note: Sushi and cocktails eighteen floors up with the best views of the three rooftops. Priciest of the group, and the food doesn't always justify it — go for the setting and a drink.
places.hours: Sun–Wed 11:00 AM – 12:00 AM · Fri–Sat until 2:00 AM

places.name: South Pointe Tavern
places.note: A proper neighborhood sports bar near the pier — the antidote to Ocean Drive. Good cocktails, games on, regulars at the bar. Pair it with South Pointe Park.

places.name: Lummus Park & the Beach
places.note: Directly across the street. Palm-shaded green strip between Ocean Drive and the sand, with a paved path for walking and biking, chair and umbrella rentals, and the best people-watching on the beach.

places.name: Official Art Deco Walking Tour
places.note: Two to two-and-a-half hours through the historic district with a guide who actually knows the architecture. Goes inside several hotel lobbies. Around $35, and the guides work for tips.

places.name: Miami Beach Sign
places.note: The colorful lettered sign at the south end of Ocean Drive. Two minutes of your time, and the obligatory group photo. Lines form midday; early morning is empty.

places.name: Miami Beach Botanical Garden
places.note: Three free acres of orchids, palms, and a Japanese garden with a koi pond. Small, quiet, and heavily shaded — the best escape from the sun and noise on the whole beach. Closed Mondays.

places.name: BouYah Watersports
places.address: 300 Alton Rd, Pier A, Miami Beach Marina
places.note: Jet skis and boat tours out of the marina, and the most consistently well-reviewed operator in an area full of shady third-party brokers. Book direct and confirm the meeting address.

places.name: Paradox Museum
places.note: Interactive optical-illusion museum in Wynwood. Roughly an hour, cheap, and a good group activity. Pair it with the Wynwood Walls murals in the same trip.

places.name: Wynwood Walls
places.note: Open-air street art in the arts district. Worth a half day off the beach — murals, breweries, and galleries in walking distance of each other.

places.name: Miami Beach Bike Rental & Segway Tours
places.note: The closest shop to the rental and the highest-volume good reviews in the area. Family run. E-bikes, regular bikes, and guided tours. Buy-two-get-one-free early bird deal comes up repeatedly in reviews.

places.name: Unlimited Biking
places.note: Confirmed e-bike inventory plus guided e-bike tours if you'd rather have someone lead. Helmets and route maps included, bikes in good shape.

places.name: Bike & Roll Miami
places.note: Bikes, rollerblades, and Segway tours. Their guided tour ranges well beyond South Beach if you want to see more of the island than the Ocean Drive strip.

places.name: SOBE Tours & Rentals
places.note: Bikes plus luggage storage, which is useful on checkout day if your flight is late. Small operation, consistently friendly reviews.

places.name: 305 Tours & Rentals
places.note: Next door to SOBE. Runs a dedicated Art Deco bike tour, which is a good way to cover the district faster than the walking tour. The Boardwalk ride north from here is the standout route.

places.name: Bikes and Segway Tours & Rentals
places.note: Very well reviewed, and they throw in free extra time and water. Also rent rollerblades. Slightly further north but on the way to the Boardwalk.

places.name: The Webster
places.note: Luxury boutique three minutes from the door. Carries designer Panama hats and fedoras alongside the rest of the collection. Designer pricing, and reviews run low on service attitude — worth a look because it is close, not because it is the best hat buy.

places.name: Heart & Soul
places.note: Small resort-wear boutique on Española Way that has historically carried affordable sunhats and Panamas. Listing shows no hours and almost no reviews, so it may not be operating — treat it as a detour on a dinner walk, not a destination.

places.name: Wanahat Miami Beach
places.note: The pick. Founded by three Ecuadorian friends selling handwoven toquilla straw hats — the real thing, sourced direct from the weavers. Staff take real time on sizing and crown shape, and the quality difference against the strip hats is visible once you try one on.

places.name: Goorin Bros
places.note: Century-old hat maker, two blocks from Wanahat on the same walk. Every style including straw fedoras and packable hats that survive a suitcase. Google lists no hours and they have moved along Lincoln Road, so call before going.

places.name: Royal Resale Boutique
places.note: Vintage, consignment, and thrift in one curated room — Chanel and Dior next to 60s and 70s pieces and a wall of designer bags. Patricia the owner does the curating herself and reviewers keep mentioning how much fun the hunt is. Open until 11 PM, closed Sundays.

places.name: URock Couture
places.note: Bold going-out pieces right on Ocean Drive, open until 1 AM. Good for a night-out outfit you cannot get at a mall. Expect $200 and up, and reviews repeatedly flag pushy or unfriendly staff — go in knowing that.

places.name: TFU TFU
places.note: Small Lincoln Road shop doing summer basics with good prints — the easiest place to grab one nice t-shirt and be done. 4.8 rating and reviewers single out the staff for being welcoming rather than hovering.
places.hours: Mon–Thu, Sat 11:00 AM – 7:00 PM · Sun 11:30 AM – 6:30 PM

places.name: Habitat Hyett
places.note: Well-curated vintage clothing plus books and home goods, next door to TFU TFU. Reviewers who shop vintage in every city rate it among the best they have seen, and prices are reasonable for the condition. Service reviews are uneven — a couple describe being ignored or profiled.

places.name: Akira
places.note: Statement pieces and going-out dresses, deep selection, open until 11 PM on weekends. The kind of place you find a Miami-night outfit that does not exist back home. Staff get named in reviews for actually helping in the fitting room.
places.hours: Mon–Thu 11:00 AM – 10:00 PM · Fri–Sat 10:00 AM – 11:00 PM

places.name: lululemon
places.note: Well stocked for the size of the chain — reviewers note it carries lines other Miami stores do not have yet, including the shoe line, plus a sale rack. Staff leave you alone until you need them.
places.hours: Mon–Sat 11:00 AM – 9:00 PM · Sun until 8:00 PM

places.name: Anthropologie
places.note: Large, airy Lincoln Road location across from lululemon — clothes, jewelry, and home goods. Recent reviews split on whether the current collection is up to standard, so treat it as a browse rather than a destination.
places.hours: Mon–Thu 10:00 AM – 8:00 PM · Fri–Sat until 9:00 PM · Sun 12:00 – 6:00 PM

places.name: Beach Boutique
places.note: A boutique in the real sense — small, tightly edited, carrying Ulla Johnson, Raquel Allegra, A Piece Apart, French swimwear, and jewelry. Patricia the owner does the styling herself. Sticker shock is part of the deal. Closed Sundays.

places.name: Free-est / Free People
places.note: Bohemian and younger than the Sunset Harbour boutiques, at more forgiving prices. Staff get repeated credit for honest fitting-room opinions and actually helping build an outfit rather than hovering. One reviewer flags a curt manager, but the floor staff reviews are consistently warm.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM · Fri–Sat until 8:00 PM

places.name: Frankie.
places.note: Curated day-to-night boutique a block from Beach Boutique, with stylists on the floor who build the outfit for you. Reviewers describe walking in with no plan and leaving with a full look in minutes. Closest thing on the beach to the Ruti model. Open Sundays, unlike its neighbor.
places.hours: Mon–Fri 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM · Sat 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM · Sun 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM

places.name: La Cubanita
places.note: Cuban food with live music and a real cocktail bar, four minutes from the door and rated 4.9 across two thousand reviews. Vaca frita and the surf and turf paella are the repeat orders. Runs to 2 AM Friday through Sunday. The easiest great dinner on this list.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11:00 AM – 12:00 AM · Fri–Sat until 2:00 AM

places.name: La Mulata
places.note: The pick for the whole group at one table. Reviewers describe parties of six being walked through the menu dish by dish, with staff adapting plates for dietary needs. Paella feeds two or three on its own. Lechón asado and vaca frita are the standouts.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 9:00 AM – 11:45 PM · Fri–Sat until 12:45 AM

places.name: Havana 1957
places.note: Cuban on Española Way, in the same block as the gelato and Mercato. The Cuban sandwich and the sampler platter are what people come back for, and the outdoor tables on the pedestrian street are the whole point. Touristy stretch, but the food holds up.

places.name: Ciao Amore Gelato
places.note: Thirty-plus gelato flavors including vegan, open until 1 AM on weekends. Sits in a touristy stretch but the gelato is the real thing — clean flavors, no artificial aftertaste. Staff let you sample your way through it. The obvious after-dinner stop on Española Way.
places.hours: Sun–Thu 8:00 AM – 12:30 AM · Fri–Sat until 1:00 AM

places.name: Matcha Maven
places.note: Tiny owner-run matcha bar in an Art Deco storefront. Ceremonial grade, organic milks, syrups made in house from whole ingredients. Rated 4.9 and regulars say the owner remembers their order. Closes at 3 PM on weekdays, so it is a morning stop.
places.hours: Mon–Fri 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM · Sat–Sun until 4:00 PM

places.name: Shepherd Artisan Coffee
places.note: Opens at 6:30 AM and runs to 9 PM — the reliable coffee and breakfast-sandwich stop, with 4.6 across four thousand reviews. Also does smoothies and pastries. Grab it and walk two blocks to the sand.

places.name: Miami Bowls
places.note: A perfect 5.0 across two thousand reviews, which almost never happens. Family run, everything made to order, and they stock protein powder and creatine as add-ons. Closes at 6 PM. The post-workout stop for whoever in the group is training.

places.name: Gymage Miami
places.note: Day passes run about $26, no membership needed. Modern, clean, well equipped, 4.8 across twelve hundred reviews. Opens at 6 AM on weekdays. Nine minutes from the door and a short walk from Miami Bowls, so the workout and the recovery bowl are one trip.
places.hours: Mon–Fri 6:00 AM – 10:00 PM · Sat–Sun 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM
